memory_update.text: NNI should be tracked as an underfollowed education infrastructure supplier: education technology services, tuition/payment processing, and loan-servicing rails may benefit from adult online and institutional program growth without owning the university brand.

LINC and UTI are not pure online universities, but their employer-linked pathways, lab capacity, OEM/corporate partnerships, and job-placement loops may represent scarcer adult-learning assets than generic online content.

The node’s likely chokepoint is a bundle: trusted employer distribution, accredited/recognized curriculum, stackable credentials, student-financing/payment infrastructure, and completion-to-job evidence.

Need a dedicated supplier pass on LMS, enrollment marketing, student-success software, assessment/proctoring, employer tuition-benefit administrators, and OPM providers; this pass surfaced stronger evidence for payments and employer-connected training operators than for niche software vendors.

node: Adult online universities and corporate-partner degree/certificate pathways
summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the universe around scarce distribution, employer-connected training capacity, payments, education technology services, and completion infrastructure for adult online and workforce-linked education. The more underfollowed exposure appears less in famous university brands and more in companies that own employer relationships, accredited delivery capacity, regulated student-payment/servicing rails, or career-training pathways that can convert adult demand into enrollments and job mobility. Candidate list is capped at four and intentionally favors small/mid-cap or niche public companies over mega-cap education technology references.
